cards.text: Friend, the LORD has just said that Cyrus, king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), will set His exiles free (Isaiah 45:13). Now the LORD keeps speaking to Israel through the prophet Isaiah. He says the products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along with the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to Israel and be theirs.

cards.question: The LORD says these nations will trudge behind Israel and come over in chains. Then what will they do?
The LORD says the nations who come over will confess that God is with Israel and that there is no other God.

cards.text: Then comes a line spoken straight to God: "Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior." Hidden, and still the Savior, friend.

cards.question: Now for the makers of idols. What does the passage say happens to them?

answers.text: They are honored by the nations

cards.question: But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an ___ salvation.

cards.text: Next comes a reminder of who's talking: the LORD, who created the heavens, formed the earth, established it, and did not create it to be empty. My whole planet is one little bakery, friend, and trust me, it is NOT empty, there's flour on every square inch.

cards.question: The LORD didn't create the earth to be empty. So what did He form it for?

cards.text: The LORD says He hasn't spoken in secret, from a place in a land of darkness, and He never told Jacob's descendants to seek Him in a wasteland. I LIVED in a land of darkness, friend, it's called the back of a junk drawer, and nobody hears a thing back there.

cards.question: The LORD says that He speaks the truth and says what is right.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out: "Come, gather together, and draw near, you fugitives from the nations." When somebody yells for the fugitives to come here, you usually RUN, friend, but this time you're being invited in.

cards.question: The LORD calls some people ignorant. Who are they?

answers.text: Those who carry idols of wood

cards.text: They carry the idol around, then pray to a god that cannot save. That's like me lugging a cookie box across the bakery and then asking the BOX to carry ME.

cards.question: The LORD says "Speak up and present your case" and then asks who foretold this long ago. What's His answer?

answers.text: It was the wise of Egypt

cards.question: In that same speech, the LORD calls Himself a righteous God and Savior.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives an invitation, and He says why: "for I am God, and there is no other." Lean in, friend, this is the big one.

cards.question: Who is the LORD calling when He says "Turn to Me and be saved"?

answers.text: All the ends of the earth

cards.text: Then the LORD swears an oath by Himself, a word that will not be revoked. Me, I promise a batch in ten minutes and my oven revokes that promise EVERY single time.

cards.question: The LORD swears: Every ___ will bow before Me, every ___ will swear allegiance.
Every knee will bow before the LORD, and surely people will say something about Him. What will they say?

answers.text: Righteousness and strength are in Him alone
He is one god among many others
Their idols can still save them too

cards.question: Everyone who rages against the LORD will stay far away from Him.
The passage ends: In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be ___ and will exult.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the LORD is 'speaking to Israel' and that the goods and the Sabeans 'will come over to Israel.' Isaiah 45:14 says only 'to you' and doesn't name who 'you' is. Cards 2 and 3 carry the same addition: 'trudge behind Israel' and 'God is with Israel.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Cush and the Sabeans appear here for the first time, but the card doesn't say who they are. Cyrus is introduced; they aren't.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'What does the passage say happens to them?' sounds like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story. No story card sets up the idol makers either: they appear for the first time in the question.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the verse's core action. Isaiah 45:18 is about the earth being formed to be inhabited, not left empty. The bakery being covered in flour is a mess, not a place being lived in, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers end in 'alone' ('The house of David alone', 'The descendants of Jacob alone'). The right answer is the only one without it, so it stands out by its pattern.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Isaiah 45:24 says those who rage against Him 'will come to Him and be put to shame.' No card ever tells the baker the 'put to shame' part. The false statement only shows that they come to Him, so the baker leaves without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank is followed by 'and will exult.' The wrong answers 'scattered' and 'forgotten' don't fit with exulting, so they aren't believable and 'justified' is the only answer that makes sense in the sentence.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.
